attachment.description: A file that travels with records in a bundle.

name.description: The file's name for people, such as access-review-q3.pdf.

domain.description: A publisher, a lowercase domain of two or more labels whose last label isn't all digits, with no scheme, port or path. At most 253 characters.

externalRef.description: A record that travels elsewhere - in another stream, or from another publisher. Never resolved inside a bundle.

publisher.description: Whose record it is, when not the publisher of this one.

revision.description: The record's revision, for types that number their revisions (such as a policy).

sha256.description: Of the record's content line, pinning exactly what it says.

feedId.description: A feed's id, <publisher>/<slug>, a domain and a slug. At most 317 characters; a reader also checks that the publisher part is a domain.

identifier.description: Something's id in one system, such as a repository in GitHub or a person in Okta. Matched exactly, both halves together.

id.description: The id in that system, as that system writes it - acme/api, 00u1ab2cd3.

system.description: Where the id comes from, in lowercase - github, gitlab, okta, entra, google, slack, serial, outpost:acme.example.

personMatch.description: What a publisher knows about the person a record is about, for a reader to match against the people it holds. Needs emails or identifiers, or both.

identifiers.description: The person's ids in other systems, matched before emails.

name.description: For people to read when resolving a match; never matched on.

app.description: The app or tool, such as track or tolerance.monorail.tools.

output.description: Which of its outputs, when it has several.

refString.description: A reference to another record, kind:key, optionally #part.

slug.description: A lowercase key made of letters, digits and single hyphens.

source.description: What the file was built from.

refs.description: Identifiers in that system, such as commit ids.

system.description: The system of record, such as track.

description: Definitions every Legible Records type can use.
title: common
